title: REAL ID Act Modification for Freely Associated States Act
official_summary:
REAL ID Act Modification for Freely Associated States Act

(Sec. 2) This bill amends the Real ID Act of 2005 to make a citizen of the Republic of the Marshall Islands, the Federated States of Micronesia, or the Republic of Palau who has been admitted to the United States as a nonimmigrant pursuant to a Compact of Free Association between the United States and the Republic or Federated States eligible for a driver's license or personal identification card. Under current law, a citizen of those countries is eligible for a temporary driver's license or personal identification card.

summary.headline: This law lets citizens of three Pacific island nations admitted under a Compact of Free Association apply for a full driver's license or ID card, not just a temporary one.
summary.what_it_does: The law changes the REAL ID Act of 2005. Before this change, citizens of the Marshall Islands, the Federated States of Micronesia, and Palau who entered the United States under a Compact of Free Association could get only a temporary driver's license or ID card. Under the new rule, they can be eligible for a regular driver's license or personal identification card.

who_it_affects.group: Citizens of the Republic of the Marshall Islands, the Federated States of Micronesia, and the Republic of Palau who were admitted to the U.S. under a Compact of Free Association
who_it_affects.how: They may now qualify for a standard driver's license or personal ID card instead of only a temporary one.

who_it_affects.group: State motor vehicle agencies that issue driver's licenses and ID cards
who_it_affects.how: They must be able to issue standard licenses and ID cards to these eligible people under the federal REAL ID framework.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The official summary does not give a separate start date. The law was enacted on December 17, 2018.
